title: TabXLLM: Unlocking Zero- and Few-Shot Tabular Prediction in LLMs via Structural-Prior Reinforcement Learning
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Permutation-based RL training turns tabular structure into dense rewards, letting one LLM beat specialized baselines across settings and domains.
layout: 3 panels: top pipeline banner left-to-right, bottom stacked bar charts plus radial charts
description: A dense three-part figure. Panel (a) is a wide top banner showing the PRPO pipeline left to right. A Tabular Pool of small table icons is sampled and permuted into a Permutation Pool of column-shuffled tables. These are combined with a question bubble and fed to a robot icon standing for the LLM. The rollout step leads to a PRPO box where six permuted tables surround the robot, each paired with reward bars. An arrow loops back for optimization. Panel (b) fills the lower left and middle with many horizontal stacked bars in blue (win), yellow (tie) and purple (loss). These compare TabXLLM with baselines under fully trained, 32-shot and zero-shot settings, split by classification and regression. Panel (c) is at the lower right and has two circular radial bar charts. They show per-domain scores for eight models, with TabXLLM in blue.
caption: (a) We collect 139 datasets to construct a PRPO-compatible reinforcement learning dataset. Each training sample is permuted into multiple variants, paired with a prediction question, and fed into TabXLLM. The rollouts generate both intra-permutation and inter-permutation rewards, providing effective optimization signals for TabXLLM. (b) Win--Tie--Loss comparison between TabXLLM and other models under fully trained, few-shot, and zero-shot settings. (c) Cross-domain performance across seven domains, illustrating the gains brought by PRPO post-training over unadapted general-purpose LLMs on the full benchmark.
abstract: Tabular prediction has long been dominated by gradient-boosted decision trees and specialized deep tabular models, while large language models (LLMs) remain difficult to make competitive despite their cross-task adaptability and transparent reasoning traces. We address this gap by incorporating tabular structural priors into LLM post-training. Specifically, we propose Permutation Relative Policy Optimization (PRPO), which operationalizes column-permutation invariance through label-preserving column permutations and two-level advantage estimation. This design converts sparse outcome rewards into denser and more stable optimization signals. Using PRPO, we develop TabXLLM, an 8B LLM for tabular prediction. Extensive experiments on 139 OpenML datasets show that TabXLLM reaches a genuinely competitive regime against strong specialized tabular baselines. It achieves strong fully supervised performance, dominates zero-shot settings, and performs on par with 32-shot strong baselines. Moreover, it substantially outperforms much larger general-purpose and reasoning LLMs, including up to a 53.17% improvement over DeepSeek-R1 (685B). These results show that structural-prior RL post-training is an effective route for making LLMs competitive in tabular prediction.
